proof_summary: Set \(m=39101\) and \(N=2\cdot100943\cdot3^{39101}-1\); an \(N+1\) primality certificate uses \(N+1=2\cdot100943\cdot3^{39101}\) and modular exponentiation of \(2+\sqrt3\) in \((\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)[\sqrt3]\).  The computations show its \((N+1)\)-st power is \(1\), while its \((N+1)/p\)-st power differs from \(1\) by a unit for \(p=2,100943,3\), forcing \(N\) to be prime and making \(m=39101\) the required counterexample.
